title: Day 1 — GPIO & Blinky
_comment: Day 1 in-class deck. AUTHORED FORWARD from the book (no PowerPoint) following
the educational patterns in AUTHORING-slides.md: do-first (run Blinky) → tour
the board (image-dominant) → walk through the code → explore the registers
(predict-then-verify) → plan the next program on paper. Activities and the
MODER table are referenced directly; the rest are <slide> blocks in ch-intro-blinky.

slides.title: GPIO & Blinky: Your First Embedded Program
slides.subtitle: ENGS 28 · Day 1 — In-Class

slides.title: Welcome to ENGS 28
items: No pre-class reading today — this is our first meeting.
You need your laptop with STM32CubeIDE installed.
You'll get a Nucleo board and a USB cable in class.
By the end of today you'll make an LED blink — and understand every line that does it.

slides.title: Today
items: Before Day 1X — plan blinkySlowToFast on paper

slides.title: Get Blinky Running
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 15 min. Do-first: get the win before any theory.

slides.presenterNote: New for most students — go slowly, take predictions out loud.

No board needed to prepare — bring your paper sketch of main().
